calls.head: Strength against strength
calls.body: The Panthers are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Senators are near the top at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Panthers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. The Senators take a lot of penalties and the Panthers draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

calls.head: Reinhart gets company tonight
calls.body: At home, the Senators keep sending Pinto’s line (Cousins, Pinto and Amadio) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Travis Green has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Panthers’ first line is Verhaeghe, Reinhart and Eller.

story.head: The Senators pile it on the Panthers
paras: Jake Sanderson was back in the lineup after missing eight games, and picked up two assists. Brady Tkachuk struck first for the Panthers on the power play midway through the first, but that’s where Florida’s luck ran out. Hayden Hodgson and Bokondji Imama dropped the gloves later in the period, and Tim Stützle tied it up for Ottawa on the power play late in the period. Claude Giroux gave the Senators the lead midway through the second. Shane Pinto stretched the lead to 3-1 late in the period. Ridly Greig and Sam Bennett squared off early in the third. Linus Ullmark left the game in the third, and Samuel Ersson finished it in net for Ottawa. Warren Foegele made it 4-1 for the Sens midway through the third, and Stephen Halliday stretched the lead to 5-1 late in the period.
The Senators drove the play, outshooting the Panthers 30-19, and the scoreboard caught up. Akira Schmid allowed five goals on 30 shots for the Panthers.
A scrum late in the first sent four players to the box. Brady Tkachuk took three penalties on his own. The Senators moved to 7-3-0, and the Panthers fell to 5-3-2.
